usage: Used for a big rock or stone in nature; it sounds a bit literary, so in everyday speech people often say 石頭 or 石塊 instead.
Common in geography and outdoor contexts, especially when talking about hills, rivers, coastlines, or dangerous rocky places.
Can appear by itself as a noun, or in compounds like 岩石 for “rock.”
Good for beginner learners to recognize in place names and written Chinese; in speech, you may hear simpler words more often.
